chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

There is no breastfeeding after weaning, no uninterrupted fasting in sawm (fasting), no orphanhood after puberty, no silence for a day until night, no reversion to Bedouin life after migration, no migration after the conquest, no divorce before marriage, no emancipation before ownership, no oath for a child alongside his parent, nor for an owned servant alongside his master, nor for a woman alongside her husband, no vow in disobedience, and no oath in severing kinship ties.

key_terms.احْتِلَامٍ: puberty marked by nocturnal emission or sexual maturity
key_terms.رَضَاعَ: breastfeeding that establishes legal nursing relations
key_terms.فِطَامٍ: weaning, after which nursing rulings no longer apply
key_terms.قَطِيعَةٍ: severing family ties or kinship relations
key_terms.نَذْرَ: a vow binding oneself to an act
key_terms.وِصَالَ: continuous fasting without breaking the fast

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith "لا رضاع بعد فطام" and related legal principles mean in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gathers a set of legal maxims and limits recognized in the sunnah (prophetic tradition), clarifying when certain rulings no longer apply or are invalid. It addresses family law, vows, oaths, fasting, social status, and kinship, showing the boundaries of valid religious commitments in Islamic law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4273 - Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"There is no breastfeeding after weaning, no continuous fasting without breaking, no orphanhood after reaching puberty, no silence for a day until night, no returning to a Bedouin life after migration, no migration after the conquest (of Mecca), no divorce before marriage, no emancipation before ownership, no oath for a child in the presence of their parent, nor for a slave with their master, nor for a woman with her husband, no vow in disobedience, and no oath in severing family ties."
